summary: Attribute encoding in service account path causes AWS->GCP role exchange failures for prod sandboxes
description: During scheduled onboarding of ephemeral sandboxes in prod-us-east, the cross-account role exchange from AWS to GCP intermittently fails. Error manifests as STS token audience mismatch and GCP WIF validation rejects the token. The root hypothesis is that the service-account path attribute inserted by the provisioner contains URL-encoded characters and a trailing slash which ends up changing the expected audience string in the STS assertion. This impacts any internal flows that use the lightweight ephemeral bridge to assume GCP-scoped service identities.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Provision ephemeral sandbox via infra-provisioner job (job id example: sandbox-provision-2026-03-08-az1)
2) Provisioner calls aws:sts:assumeRoleWithSAML / assume-role-to-gcp flow to generate short-lived creds
3) Attempt exchange to GCP via workload-identity-federation with asserted audience matching '//' + project + '/serviceAccounts/' + path
4) Observe WIF validation error: 'audience mismatch' or 'invalid token audience' and request fails with 403 from token exchange endpoint.
logs:
[2026-03-08T16:04:22Z] provisioner: starting exchange for sandbox id sandbox-provision-2026-03-08-az1
[2026-03-08T16:04:23Z] aws-sts: assume-role success, token_audience='https://iam.googleapis.com/projects/_/serviceAccounts/project@example.iam.gserviceaccount.com/'
[2026-03-08T16:04:23Z] gcp-wif: token validation failed: audience 'https://iam.googleapis.com/projects/_/serviceAccounts/project%2Fteam%2Fservice-account/' does not match expected 'https://iam.googleapis.com/projects/_/serviceAccounts/project/team/service-account'
[2026-03-08T16:04:23Z] provisioner: exchange failed, rolling back resources
Note: token shows URL-encoded slashes "%2F" and a trailing slash in some runs.
investigation_notes:
Initial reproduction limited to prod-us-east sandboxes created by the new provisioner refactor (infra PR 4821). Reproduced consistently when service account path contains nested namespace segments (e.g., 'project/team/service-account').
Hypothesis: our audience string builder escapes path segments which causes STS to emit an audience with percent-encoding. GCP WIF expects the canonical, unencoded path. Two possible fixes: (A) normalize audience to unencoded form before sending to GCP; (B) change AWS-side issuance to use unencoded audience identical to GCP expectation.
Observed variance: older provisioner runs (pre-PR 4821) did not include encoded segments and succeeded. This aligns with a recent template change inserting urlencode(path_segment) by default.
Telemetry: injected additional debug logging in provisioner to capture raw path and final audience; sample traces and logs uploaded to internal S3: s3://redwood-infra-debug/provisioner/INT-178933/2026-03-08/trace.log
Temporary mitigation tested: strip trailing slash and percent-decode audience string before calling GCP; small patch in provisioner reduced failures in limited canary runs.
comments: 2026-03-09 - Priya Singh (SRE): Noticed spikes in sandbox creation errors yesterday. Correlated with infra PR 4821 merge. Adding gcp-wif and cloud-provisioner teams.

2026-03-10 - Devon Reed (Assignee): I reproduced locally using the provisioner job. The path builder added encodeURIComponent() -> percent-encode. WIF rejects percent-encoded audience. Preparing hotfix branch to decode audience before exchange.

2026-03-11 - Marco Liu (Security): Confirmed WIF validation is strict about audience equality. Decoding audience is acceptable but ensure we don't open a canonicalization bug where two distinct service-account paths collapse. Recommend add unit tests around path normalization.

2026-03-12 - Ava Martinez (Reporter): Customer-facing teams reported 7 sandbox failures affecting ephemeral debugging windows this week. Priority raised because this blocks quick-boot developer sandboxes.

2026-03-14 - Devon Reed: Hotfix branch infra/pipeline/bugfix/normalize-audience (PR 4837) created. Ran canary of 25 sandboxes, 1 failure unrelated (DNS timeout). Planning staged rollout across prod-us-east tomorrow morning 03:00 UTC.

2026-03-14 - QA (Automated): Canary run metrics: success rate 98/100. Verified token audiences are unencoded and match expected GCP canonical format. Added regression tests for paths with percent-encoded characters.\n
resolution: Hotfix applied: provisioner now percent-decodes audience fragments and strips trailing slashes before performing WIF exchange. Deployed to prod-us-east during low-traffic window. Post-deploy monitoring for 24h showed sandbox creation error rate back to baseline. Follow-up task created to harden audience construction in the shared auth library and add unit/integration tests.
